story.text: 게이트를 나서자마자, 익숙한 목소리가 들려왔다. '야, 너 왜 이렇게 늦게 나와.' 용우가 팔짱을 끼고 서 있었다.
story.reading: ge-i-teu-reul na-seo-ja-ma-ja, ik-suk-an mok-so-ri-ga deul-lyeo-wat-da. ya, neo wae i-reo-ke neut-ge na-wa. yong-u-ga pal-jjang-eul kki-go seo iss-eot-da.
story.en: The moment I stepped out of the gate, a familiar voice called out. 'Hey, why are you so late.' Yongwoo stood there with his arms crossed.

story.text: '캐리어 바퀴 하나는 또 왜 저래. 너 진짜 또 칠칠맞게 굴지 마라. 내가 몇 번을 말해.'
story.reading: kae-ri-eo ba-kwi ha-na-neun tto wae jeo-rae. neo jin-jja tto chil-chil-mat-ge gul-ji ma-ra. nae-ga myeot beon-eul mal-hae.
story.en: 'What's wrong with one of your suitcase wheels again. Seriously, don't be so careless again. How many times do I have to tell you.'

story.text: 쉬는 날인데도 굳이 마중을 나온 걸 아니까, 고맙다고 하려는데 용우가 먼저 말을 자른다. '착각하지 마라. 지나가는 길이었다.'
story.reading: swi-neun nal-in-de-do gud-i ma-jung-eul na-on geol a-ni-kka, go-map-da-go ha-ryeo-neun-de yong-u-ga meon-jeo mal-eul ja-reun-da. chak-gak-a-ji ma-ra. ji-na-ga-neun gil-i-eot-da.
story.en: I knew he'd come out to meet me even on his day off, and I was about to say thanks, but Yongwoo cut me off first. 'Don't get the wrong idea. I just happened to be passing by.'

story.text: 말은 그렇게 하면서 벌써 짐을 양손 가득 들고 앞장서 걷고 있다. 뒷모습이 꼭 오빠 같다.
story.reading: mal-eun geu-reo-ke ha-myeon-seo beol-sseo jim-eul yang-son ga-deuk deul-go ap-jang-seo geot-go it-da. dwit-mo-seub-i kkok o-ppa gat-da.
story.en: Even as he says that, he's already walking ahead with both hands full of my luggage. From behind, he looks just like an older brother.

story.text: '여권은. 지갑은. 핸드폰 배터리는 챙겼어?' 차에 타기도 전에 확인 목록이 끝도 없다.
story.reading: yeo-gwon-eun. ji-gab-eun. haen-deu-pon bae-teo-ri-neun chaeng-gyeoss-eo? cha-e ta-gi-do jeon-e hwak-in mok-rok-i kkeut-do eop-da.
story.en: 'Your passport. Your wallet. Did you charge your phone battery?' The checklist goes on before I've even gotten in the car.

story.text: '그만 좀 물어봐, 잔소리쟁이.' 웃으며 놀리자 용우가 살짝 눈을 흘긴다. '이게 잔소리로 보이나. 걱정이지.'
story.reading: geu-man jom mul-eo-bwa, jan-so-ri-jaeng-i. us-eu-myeo nol-li-ja yong-u-ga sal-jjak nun-eul heul-gin-da. i-ge jan-so-ri-ro bo-i-na. geok-jeong-i-ji.
story.en: 'Stop asking already, you nag.' I teased him with a laugh, and Yongwoo shot me a look. 'You call this nagging? It's called worrying.'

story.text: 차 문을 열어주며 용우가 씩 웃는다. '일단 타라. 오늘 대화 몇 개 들려줄 테니까, 잘 듣고 무슨 상황인지 맞혀봐라.'
story.reading: cha mun-eul yeol-eo-ju-myeo yong-u-ga ssik us-neun-da. il-dan ta-ra. o-neul dae-hwa myeot gae deul-lyeo-jul te-ni-kka, jal deut-go mu-seun sang-hwang-in-ji mac-hyeo-bwa-ra.
story.en: Yongwoo grins as he opens the car door for me. 'Get in first. I'll play you a couple of conversations today — listen carefully and figure out what's going on.'

words.example: 짐을 자꾸 흘리고 다니다니, 진짜 칠칠맞구나.
words.example_reading: jim-eul ja-kku heul-li-go da-ni-da-ni, jin-jja chil-chil-mat-gu-na
words.example_en: Dropping your things all over the place like that — you're really careless.

words.meaning: Going out to meet/greet someone arriving
words.example_en: Even though he was busy, he came all the way to the airport to meet me.
Your luggage looks heavy, so let me carry it.

words.meaning: To look after, take care of, pack/prepare
words.example_en: Grab your passport before we leave.

words.example: 잔소리처럼 들려도 다 널 위해서 하는 말이야.
words.example_reading: jan-so-ri-cheo-reom deul-lyeo-do da neol wi-hae-seo ha-neun mal-i-ya
words.example_en: Even if it sounds like nagging, I'm only saying it for your sake.

sentences.ko: 공항에 마중 나온 용우는 팔짱을 낀 채 나를 기다리고 있었다.
sentences.reading: gong-hang-e ma-jung na-on yong-u-neun pal-jjang-eul kkin chae na-reul gi-da-ri-go iss-eot-da
sentences.en: Yongwoo, who'd come to meet me at the airport, was waiting for me with his arms crossed.

sentences.ko: 그는 잔소리를 하면서도 이미 내 짐을 양손 가득 들고 있었다.
sentences.reading: geu-neun jan-so-ri-reul ha-myeon-seo-do i-mi nae jim-eul yang-son ga-deuk deul-go iss-eot-da
sentences.en: Even while nagging, he was already carrying my luggage with both hands.

sentences.ko: 여권이랑 지갑은 잘 챙겼냐고 그는 차에 타기도 전에 물었다.
sentences.reading: yeo-gwon-i-rang ji-gab-eun jal chaeng-gyeon-nya-go geu-neun cha-e ta-gi-do jeon-e mul-eot-da
sentences.en: He asked if I'd properly packed my passport and wallet before we'd even gotten in the car.

sentences.ko: 또 칠칠맞게 짐을 흘리고 다니지 말라고 그는 몇 번이나 말했다.
sentences.reading: tto chil-chil-mat-ge jim-eul heul-li-go da-ni-ji mal-la-go geu-neun myeot beon-i-na mal-haet-da
sentences.en: He told me over and over not to be careless and drop my things again.

sentences.ko: 걱정이지 잔소리가 아니라며 그는 살짝 눈을 흘겼다.
sentences.reading: geok-jeong-i-ji jan-so-ri-ga a-ni-ra-myeo geu-neun sal-jjak nun-eul heul-gyeot-da
sentences.en: He shot me a look, saying it was worry, not nagging.

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 야, 짐은 그거 다야? 무거워 보이는데 내가 들게.
turns.reading: ya, jim-eun geu-geo da-ya? mu-geo-wo bo-i-neun-de nae-ga deul-ge.
turns.en: Hey, is that all your luggage? Looks heavy, let me carry it.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.text: 괜찮아요, 저 혼자 들 수 있어요.
turns.reading: gwaen-chan-a-yo, jeo hon-ja deul su iss-eo-yo.
turns.en: It's fine, I can carry it myself.

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 됐고, 이리 줘봐. 너 팔 힘도 없으면서 또 무리하지 말고.
turns.reading: dwaet-go, i-ri jwo-bwa. neo pal him-do eops-eu-myeon-seo tto mu-ri-ha-ji mal-go.
turns.en: Never mind, just hand it over. You've got no arm strength, don't push yourself.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.reading: go-ma-wo-yo. geu-reon-de o-neul swi-neun nal a-ni-eoss-eo-yo?
turns.en: …Thanks. But wasn't today your day off?

dialogues.question: 용우가 손님의 짐을 직접 들어준 이유는 무엇인가요?
dialogues.question_en: Why did Yongwoo carry the passenger's luggage himself?
dialogues.explanation: 용우는 손님이 무거운 짐을 혼자 드는 걸 걱정해 먼저 나서서 짐을 들어주었습니다.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.text: 기장님, 저 여권이랑 지갑 잘 챙겼는지 다시 확인해봐야겠어요.
turns.reading: gi-jang-nim, jeo yeo-gwon-i-rang ji-gap jal chaeng-gyeon-neun-ji da-si hwak-in-hae-bwa-ya-gess-eo-yo.
turns.en: Captain, I should double check I've got my passport and wallet.

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 그러니까 내가 아까부터 물어봤잖아. 미리미리 좀 챙겨라.
turns.reading: geu-reo-ni-kka nae-ga a-kka-bu-teo mul-eo-bwat-jan-a. mi-ri-mi-ri jom chaeng-gyeo-ra.
turns.en: That's why I kept asking earlier. Take care of things ahead of time.

turns.speaker: 손님
turns.en: Stop nagging, I'm a grown-up, you know?

turns.speaker: 권용우 기장
turns.text: 다 컸어도 허당인 건 여전하네. 이게 잔소리로 보이면 어쩔 수 없고.
turns.reading: da keoss-eo-do heo-dang-in geon yeo-jeon-ha-ne. i-ge jan-so-ri-ro bo-i-myeon eo-jjeol su eop-go.
turns.en: Grown-up or not, you're still scatterbrained. If this looks like nagging to you, so be it.

dialogues.question: 용우가 손님에게 여권과 지갑을 확인하라고 한 이유는 무엇인가요?
dialogues.question_en: Why did Yongwoo tell the passenger to check her passport and wallet?
dialogues.correct_answer: 손님이 물건을 잘 못 챙길까 봐 걱정돼서
options: 손님이 물건을 잘 못 챙길까 봐 걱정돼서
dialogues.explanation: 용우는 손님이 덜렁대는 성격을 알기에 미리 여권과 지갑을 챙기라고 잔소리했습니다.
